text.p: These are the leading stories in the Zimbabwe press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The Zimbabwe Electricity Supply Authority (ZESA) board is seeking an urgent meeting with President Robert Mugabe to have the sale of ZESA's Hwange Thermal power station to a Malaysian company, YTL Corporation Berhard cancelled, warning that the deal has serious political and economic repercussions for the government.

- The National Railways of Zimbabwe is heading for a loss of nearly Z$196 million in the 1995/96 financial year and the deficit could soar up to Z$334 in the current year, the parastatal's latest preliminary and unaudited results show.

- The newly appointed International Monetary Fund (IMF) resident representative in Zimbabwe, Robert Franco, says the Southern African country has the infrastructure it needs to succeed with economic reforms.
- Zimbabwe's Export Processing Zone Authority will not waive the requirement that companies should export at least 80 percent of their total production to qualify for EPZ status.
- Zimbabwe's privatisation programme is set to gather momentum once a document on the programme is approved by cabinet.

- The $26 million vote allocated Zimbabwe's sport, recreation and Culture ministry for the 1996/97 fiscal year was passed in parliament amid strong resistance from some members who felt an audit report of the 1995 Sixth All Africa Games needed to be presented first.
- The two Fokker 50 aircraft leased by Air Zimbabwe from the now-liquidated Fokker Aircraft BV Manufacturers of the Netherlands will go out of operation at the end of October.
